_what: Notes on how the certified engine builds the PolicyEngine counterpart in lane uk-childcare-100k (CenTax and CBP claims alike), and what was verified about each certified pair the lane has run. Each note cites the engine file it was read from and names, in variants, the pairs it was checked on; it attaches only to those pairs' results. verified_pairs holds each pair's own statements; ingest refuses an artifact whose pair is not listed, so no note written for one pair attaches to another. The measured numbers that go with them are written onto each result by scorecard_db/ingest_uk_childcare_100k.py from the artifact beside this file, not copied here.

annotations.text: Both offers are England's. policyengine-uk 2.89.2 tests country == ENGLAND for the extended, universal and targeted hours but not for Tax-Free Childcare, which it applies across the UK. The counterpart sums each head for people in English households (the household's country projected onto its members); ingest checks that no free-hours head moves outside England, and states the Tax-Free Childcare change outside England.
annotations.basis: policyengine_uk 2.89.2 variables/gov/dfe/extended_childcare_entitlement/extended_childcare_entitlement_eligible.py, universal_childcare_entitlement/universal_childcare_entitlement_eligible.py and targeted_childcare_entitlement/targeted_childcare_entitlement_eligible.py (in_england); variables/gov/hmrc/tax_free_childcare/ (no country test); pipeline/compute_uk_childcare_100k.py england_masks; results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json sums_gbp_england

annotations.text: policyengine-uk 2.89.2 switches a child's universal and targeted hours off once the family is eligible for the extended hours, and values the extended hours at the family's drawn weekly usage (maximum_extended_childcare_hours_usage). The counterpart sums all three entitlements, so the universal hours a newly eligible family loses are netted out rather than double-counted. policyengine-uk#2177 (merged 12 October 2026, after the pin) changed this, closing policyengine-uk#1930.

The offer starts at 9 months. The engine's extended-hours scale starts at age 0.75, but every age on this pair is a whole number of years, so a child under 1 has age 0 and no child under 1 receives extended hours in any world or year (both measured). microcosm#1126 records the same for the Microcosm release.
annotations.basis: policyengine_uk 2.89.2 parameters/gov/dfe/extended_childcare_entitlement/hours.yaml (threshold 0.75 from 2025); results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json counts.people_with_fractional_age and counts.children_under_one_receiving_extended (0 in every world and year); https://github.com/PolicyEngine/microcosm/issues/1126

Two smaller PolicyEngine-side factors are recorded on the result: the universal-hours switch-off (policyengine-uk#1930, changed after the pin by policyengine-uk#2177) and no hours for children under 1.
